time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 at t = 0
units: pixels and seconds; image x to the right, y downward; no metric scale recorded

camera.motion: static (uniform grey background RGB ~194, no texture; nothing to pan against, and no evidence of camera motion)
camera.view: bird seen from directly above/below (top-down planar view); motion in the image plane
camera.perspective_cues: none (no ground, horizon or vanishing points); single depth plane -> one metres-per-pixel scale

objects.name: phoenix
objects.description: the only object: a phoenix / peacock-like bird with green-purple-dark wings, dark green body spine and long orange peacock-eye tail feathers; head (beak) points LEFT, tail right
objects.visible_frames: 0-71 (fully in frame 0-69; frames 70-71 head/beak leaves the left edge, x-extent cut)
objects.reference_point: ref_x, ref_y: beak tip x and spine (body axis) row; beak tip moves rigidly with body (checked by template matching, agreement ~1-3 px/frame). Origin of the rig is an unknown fixed offset behind the beak along the spine (wing roots are ~200-270 px behind the beak tip); this offset does not affect displacements/speeds.
objects.motion: flies horizontally LEFT along y ~ 720-729 px, accelerating overall, with a flapping-dependent speed ripple

extents_px.length_x_beak_to_tail_tip: 690-746 (varies with tail pose; median ~715; frames 0-69 only)
extents_px.note: span_y_px is the full vertical mask extent (wing tip to wing tip, or tail feathers when wings are folded)

flap_cycle.note: pattern repeats every 25 frames (~1.04 s); two span peaks per cycle (930 px and 1008 px)

events.event: phoenix visible, nearly stationary (dx 0 px between frames 0 and 1), then starts moving left
local speed minimum (beak dx ~1-3 px/frame), also at frame 20
beak/head crosses the left image edge (x-extent cut from here)

files.tracks/phoenix_body_shift.csv: per-frame body template shift (cross-check / extrapolation for frames 70-71)
